record.context_brief: Representations of integers by sums and differences of primes
record.original_question: For integers k > 3 and 1 < s < k, can every odd integer (when k is odd) or every even integer (when k is even) be represented as a sum of k-s primes minus a sum of s distinct other primes, does the statement remain true when all k primes are required to be distinct, and in how many ways can each target integer be represented in this form?

evidence.quote: (ii) Is the conjecture true when all the k prime numbers are different?  (iii) In how many ways can each odd integer be expressed as above?
(v) Is the conjecture true when all the k prime numbers are different?  (vi) In how many ways can each even integer be expressed as above?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let k and s be integers with k > 3 and 1 < s < k. Consider representations of an integer N in the form
    N = (p_1 + p_2 + ... + p_{k-s}) - (q_1 + q_2 + ... + q_s),
where p_1, ..., p_{k-s} and q_1, ..., q_s are prime numbers.

(a) Prove or disprove the following: if k is odd, then every odd integer N can be represented in the above form, and if k is even, then every even integer N can be represented in the above form, where the primes p_i are allowed to repeat among themselves and the primes q_j are required to be distinct from one another (and distinct from the p_i, in the sense intended for "other primes").

(b) Determine whether the statement in (a) remains true under the stronger requirement that all k primes p_1, ..., p_{k-s}, q_1, ..., q_s are pairwise distinct.

(c) For each admissible target integer N (odd if k is odd, even if k is even), determine the number of representations of N in the form above (with the distinctness conditions as in (a) and as in (b)).
artifact.status_search_result: No source addressing this specific Goldbach-type representation problem (sums of k−s primes minus sums of s primes, with the distinctness variants and counting questions) was found. Even the classical binary Goldbach conjecture and exact counting formulas for Goldbach-type representations remain unresolved, so these stronger/related questions are also open.

status_evidence.title: Goldbach's conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The (binary) Goldbach conjecture remains unproven; only the ternary (weak) version was proved by Helfgott.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational Goldbach-type questions about representing integers by sums of primes remain open, suggesting the present generalization is at least as open.

status_evidence.title: Goldbach's weak conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Every odd number greater than 5 is the sum of three primes (Helfgott, 2013).
status_evidence.claim: Only specific small-k positive cases of Goldbach-type representation conjectures are known; counting and distinct-prime variants are not established in general.
